title: Shimaya Ichizaemon surveys the Bonin Islands, 1675
summary: The shogunate sent Shimaya Ichizaemon to survey the uninhabited islands that castaways had reported. He left Shimoda on 5 April 1675 by way of Hachijōjima, sighted Chichijima on 29 April, landed on 1 May and spent about a month surveying Chichijima and Hahajima, naming the islands and raising a shrine marked as part of Great Japan.

legs.source: Ogasawara (Sasakawa Peace Foundation): left Shimoda on 5 April, by way of Hachijōjima
legs.note: Both ports are named; the track between them is drawn by the editor.

legs.source: Ogasawara (Sasakawa Peace Foundation): found Chichijima on 29 April and anchored at Futami harbour
legs.note: The open-sea track is drawn by the editor. The page does not describe the way home.

events.label: Futami harbour, Chichijima
events.text: He found Chichijima on 29 April and first landed on 1 May. The crew measured the islands’ sizes, latitude and distances from Shimoda, Hachijōjima and Miyakejima. He named Chichijima, Hahajima, Anijima, Ototojima, Anejima and Imotojima, and places called Ōmura, Okumura and Susaki.

events.label: A shrine: “Part of Great Japan”
events.text: He built a shrine invoking Hachiman Daibosatsu, Amaterasu Omikami and Kasuga Myōjin; its side inscription reads “Dai Nippon no Uchi nari”. He let loose three roosters and two hens, and took mountain betel palms, mulberry logs and birds back for the shogunate.

events.label: Hahajima surveyed
events.text: The month on the islands took in Hahajima as well as Chichijima. His notes survive in the Historical Records of the Ogasawara Islands.
